verses.text_uthmani: طه

trs.20: Ṭā, Hā.<sup foot_note=196741>1</sup>
trs.85: Ta Ha
trs.22: Ta-Ha.
trs.203: Tâ-Hâ.

verses.text_uthmani: مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰٓ

trs.20: We have not sent down to you the Qur’ān that you be distressed
trs.85: It was not to distress you [Prophet] that We sent down the Quran to you,
trs.22: We have not sent down the Qur'an to thee to be (an occasion) for thy distress,
trs.203: We have not sent down the Qur’ân unto you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) to cause you distress,

verses.text_uthmani: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ

trs.20: But only as a reminder for those who fear [Allāh] -
trs.85: but as a reminder for those who hold God in awe,
trs.22: But only as an admonition to those who fear (Allah),-
trs.203: But only as a Reminder to those who fear (Allâh).

verses.text_uthmani: تَنزِيلًا مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى

trs.20: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens,
trs.85: a revelation from the One who created the earth and the high heaven,
trs.22: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the heavens on high.
trs.203: A revelation from Him (Allâh) Who has created the earth and high heavens.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ

trs.20: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.<sup foot_note=196742>1</sup>
trs.85: the Lord of Mercy, established on the throne.
trs.22: (Allah) Most Gracious is firmly established on the throne (of authority).
trs.203: The Most Gracious (Allâh) rose over (Istawâ) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty).

verses.text_uthmani: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ

trs.20: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.
trs.85: Everything in the heavens and on earth, everything between them, everything beneath the soil, belongs to Him.
trs.22: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and on earth, and all between them, and all beneath the soil.
trs.203: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and all that is between them, and all that is under the soil.

verses.text_uthmani: وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى

trs.20: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
trs.85: Whatever you may say aloud, He knows what you keep secret and what is even more hidden.
trs.22: If thou pronounce the word aloud, (it is no matter): for verily He knoweth what is secret and what is yet more hidden.
trs.203: And if you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) speak (the invocation) aloud, then verily, He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

trs.20: Allāh - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
trs.85: God––there is no god but Him––the most excellent names belong to Him.
trs.22: Allah! there is no god but He! To Him belong the most Beautiful Names.
trs.203: Allâh! Lâ ilâha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He)! To Him belong the Best Names.<sup foot_note=154713>1</sup>

verses.text_uthmani: وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ

trs.20: And has the story of Moses reached you? -
trs.85: Has the story of Moses come to you [Prophet]?
trs.22: Has the story of Moses reached thee?
trs.203: And has there come to you the story of Mûsâ (Moses)?

verses.text_uthmani: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى

trs.20: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."
trs.85: He saw a fire and said to his people, ‘Stay here––I can see a fire. Maybe I can bring you a flaming brand from it or find some guidance there.’
trs.22: Behold, he saw a fire: So he said to his family, "Tarry ye; I perceive a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire."
trs.203: When he saw a fire, he said to his family: "Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire."

verses.text_uthmani: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰٓ

trs.20: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses,
trs.85: When he came to the fire, he was summoned, ‘Moses!
trs.22: But when he came to the fire, a voice was heard: "O Moses!
trs.203: And when he came to it (the fire), he was called by name: "O Mûsâ (Moses)!

verses.text_uthmani: إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى

trs.20: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the blessed valley of Ṭuwā.
trs.85: I am your Lord. Take off your shoes: you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
trs.22: "Verily I am thy Lord! therefore (in My presence) put off thy shoes: thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa.
trs.203: "Verily I am your Lord! So take off your shoes; you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa.

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ

trs.20: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
trs.85: I have chosen you, so listen to what is being revealed.
trs.22: "I have chosen thee: listen, then, to the inspiration (sent to thee).
trs.203: "And I have chosen you. So listen to that which will be revealed (to you).

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ

trs.20: Indeed, I am Allāh. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
trs.85: I am God; there is no god but Me. So worship Me and keep up the prayer so that you remember Me.
trs.22: "Verily, I am Allah: There is no god but I: So serve thou Me (only), and establish regular prayer for celebrating My praise.
trs.203: "Verily! I am Allâh! Lâ ilâha illa Ana (none has the right to be worshipped but I), so worship Me, and perform As-Salât (Iqâmat-as-Salât) for My Remembrance.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ

trs.20: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it<sup foot_note=196743>1</sup> - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
trs.85: The Hour is coming––though I choose to keep it hidden––for each soul to be rewarded for its labour.
trs.22: "Verily the Hour is coming - My design is to keep it hidden - for every soul to receive its reward by the measure of its Endeavour.
trs.203: "Verily, the Hour is coming - and I am almost hiding it from Myself - that every person may be rewarded for that which he strives.

verses.text_uthmani: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرْدَىٰ

trs.20: So do not let one avert you from it<sup foot_note=196744>1</sup> who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish.
trs.85: Do not let anyone who does not believe in it and follows his own desires distract you from it, and so bring you to ruin.’
trs.22: "Therefore let not such as believe not therein but follow their own lusts, divert thee therefrom, lest thou perish!"..
trs.203: "Therefore, let not the one who believes not therein (i.e. in the Day of Resurrection, Reckoning, Paradise and Hell.), but follows his own lusts,<sup foot_note=154714>1</sup> divert you therefrom, lest you perish.

verses.text_uthmani: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?"
trs.85: ‘Moses, what is that in your right hand?’
trs.22: "And what is that in the right hand, O Moses?"
trs.203: "And what is that in your right hand, O Mûsâ (Moses)?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ

trs.20: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses."
trs.85: ‘It is my staff,’ he said, ‘I lean on it; restrain my sheep with it; I also have other uses for it.’
trs.22: He said, "It is my rod: on it I lean; with it I beat down fodder for my flocks; and in it I find other uses."
trs.203: He said: "This is my stick, whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "Throw it down, O Moses."
trs.85: God said, ‘Throw it down, Moses.’
trs.22: (Allah) said, "Throw it, O Moses!"
trs.203: (Allâh) said: "Cast it down, O Mûsâ (Moses)!"

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَىٰ

trs.20: So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly.
trs.85: He threw it down and- lo and behold!- it became a fast-moving snake.
trs.22: He threw it, and behold! It was a snake, active in motion.
trs.203: He cast it down, and behold! It was a snake, moving quickly.

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.
trs.85: He said, ‘Pick it up without fear: We shall turn it back into its former state.
trs.22: (Allah) said, "Seize it, and fear not: We shall return it at once to its former condition"..
trs.203: Allâh said: "Grasp it and fear not; We shall return it to its former state,

verses.text_uthmani: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ

trs.20: And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign,
trs.85: Now place your hand under your armpit and it will come out white, though unharmed: that is another sign.
trs.22: "Now draw thy hand close to thy side: It shall come forth white (and shining), without harm (or stain),- as another Sign,-
trs.203: "And press your (right) hand to your (left) side: it will come forth white (and shining), without any disease as another sign,

verses.text_uthmani: لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى

trs.20: That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.
trs.85: We do this to show you some of Our greatest signs.
trs.22: "In order that We may show thee (two) of our Greater Signs.
trs.203: "That We may show you (some) of Our Greater Signs.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ

trs.20: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed [i.e., tyrannized]."
trs.85: Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly become a tyrant.’
trs.22: "Go thou to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds."
trs.203: "Go to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)! Verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience, and has behaved as an arrogant and as a tyrant)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى

trs.20: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]
trs.85: Moses said, ‘Lord, lift up my heart
trs.22: (Moses) said: "O my Lord! expand me my breast;
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "O my Lord! Open for me my chest (grant me self-confidence, contentment, and boldness).

verses.text_uthmani: وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى

trs.20: And ease for me my task
trs.85: and ease my task for me.
trs.22: "Ease my task for me;
trs.203: "And ease my task for me;

verses.text_uthmani: وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى

trs.20: And untie the knot from my tongue
trs.85: Untie my tongue,
trs.22: "And remove the impediment from my speech,
trs.203: "And loose the knot (the defect) from my tongue, (i.e. remove the incorrectness from my speech) [That occurred as a result of a brand of fire which Mûsâ (Moses) put in his mouth when he was an infant]. (Tafsir At-Tabarî).

verses.text_uthmani: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى

trs.20: That they may understand my speech.
trs.85: so that they may understand my words,
trs.22: "So they may understand what I say:
trs.203: "That they understand my speech.

verses.text_uthmani: وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى

trs.20: And appoint for me a minister [i.e., assistant] from my family -
trs.85: and give me a helper from my family,
trs.22: "And give me a Minister from my family,
trs.203: "And appoint for me a helper from my family,

verses.text_uthmani: هَـٰرُونَ أَخِى

trs.20: Aaron, my brother.
trs.85: my brother Aaron-
trs.22: "Aaron, my brother;
trs.203: "Hârûn (Aaron), my brother.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى

trs.20: Increase through him my strength
trs.85: augment my strength through him.
trs.22: "Add to my strength through him,
trs.203: "Increase my strength with him,

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى

trs.20: And let him share my task
trs.85: Let him share my task
trs.22: "And make him share my task:
trs.203: "And let him share my task (of conveying Allâh’s Message and Prophethood),

verses.text_uthmani: كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا

trs.20: That we may exalt You much
trs.85: so that we can glorify You much
trs.22: "That we may celebrate Thy praise without stint,
trs.203: "That we may glorify You much,

verses.text_uthmani: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا

trs.20: And remember You much.
trs.85: and remember You often:
trs.22: "And remember Thee without stint:
trs.203: "And remember You much,

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا

trs.20: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."
trs.85: You are always watching over us.’
trs.22: "For Thou art He that (ever) regardeth us."
trs.203: "Verily You are Ever a Well-Seer of us."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses.
trs.85: God said, ‘Moses, your request is granted.
trs.22: (Allah) said: "Granted is thy prayer, O Moses!"
trs.203: (Allâh) said: "You are granted your request, O Mûsâ (Moses)!

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ

trs.20: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time,
trs.85: Indeed We showed you favour before.
trs.22: "And indeed We conferred a favour on thee another time (before).
trs.203: "And indeed We conferred a favour on you another time (before).

verses.text_uthmani: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ

trs.20: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired,
trs.85: We inspired your mother, saying,
trs.22: "Behold! We sent to thy mother, by inspiration, the message:
trs.203: "When We inspired your mother with that which We inspired.

verses.text_uthmani: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ ۚ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

trs.20: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me<sup foot_note=196745>1</sup> that you would be brought up under My eye [i.e., observation and care].
trs.85: “Put your child into the chest, then place him in the river. Let the river wash him on to its bank, and he will be taken in by an enemy of Mine and his.” I showered you with My love and planned that you should be reared under My watchful eye.
trs.22: "'Throw (the child) into the chest, and throw (the chest) into the river: the river will cast him up on the bank, and he will be taken up by one who is an enemy to Me and an enemy to him': But I cast (the garment of) love over thee from Me: and (this) in order that thou mayest be reared under Mine eye.
trs.203: "Saying: ‘Put him (the child) into the Tabût (a box or a case or a chest) and put it into the river (Nile); then the river shall cast it up on the bank, and there, an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his shall take him.’ And I endued you with love from Me, in order that you may be brought up under My Eye.

translation.text: and that you may be brought up

verses.text_uthmani: إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ ۖ فَرَجَعْنَـٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ ۚ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَـٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّـٰكَ فُتُونًا ۚ فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone,<sup foot_note=196746>1</sup> but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
trs.85: Your sister went out, saying, “I will tell you someone who will nurse him,” then We returned you to your mother so that she could rejoice and not grieve. Later you killed a man, but We saved you from distress and tried you with other tests. You stayed among the people of Midian for years, then you came here as I ordained.
trs.22: "Behold! thy sister goeth forth and saith, 'shall I show you one who will nurse and rear the (child)?' So We brought thee back to thy mother, that her eye might be cooled and she should not grieve. Then thou didst slay a man, but We saved thee from trouble, and We tried thee in various ways. Then didst thou tarry a number of years with the people of Midian. Then didst thou come hither as ordained, O Moses!
trs.203: "When your sister went and said: ‘Shall I show you one who will nurse him?’ So We restored you to your mother, that she might cool her eyes and she should not grieve. Then you did kill a man, but We saved you from great distress and tried you with a heavy trial. Then you stayed a number of years with the people of Madyan (Midian). Then you came here according to the fixed term which I ordained (for you), O Mûsâ (Moses)!

verses.text_uthmani: وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى

trs.20: And I produced you for Myself.<sup foot_note=196747>1</sup>
trs.85: I have chosen you for Myself.
trs.22: "And I have prepared thee for Myself (for service)"..
trs.203: "And I have chosen you,<sup foot_note=154715>1</sup> for Myself.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكْرِى

trs.20: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
trs.85: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and make sure that you remember Me.
trs.22: "Go, thou and thy brother, with My Signs, and slacken not, either of you, in keeping Me in remembrance.
trs.203: "Go you and your brother with My Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), and do not, you both, slacken and become weak in My Remembrance.

verses.text_uthmani: ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ

trs.20: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
trs.85: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has exceeded all bounds.
trs.22: "Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds;
trs.203: "Go, both of you, to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience and behaved as an arrogant and as a tyrant).

verses.text_uthmani: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ

trs.20: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allāh]."
trs.85: Speak to him gently so that he may take heed, or show respect.’
trs.22: "But speak to him mildly; perchance he may take warning or fear (Allah)."
trs.203: "And speak to him mildly, perhaps he may accept admonition or fear (Allâh)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ

trs.20: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
trs.85: They said, ‘Lord, we fear he will do us great harm or exceed all bounds.’
trs.22: They (Moses and Aaron) said: "Our Lord! We fear lest he hasten with insolence against us, or lest he transgress all bounds."
trs.203: They said: "Our Lord! Verily we fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (all bounds against us)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.
trs.85: He said, ‘Do not be afraid, I am with you both, hearing and seeing everything.
trs.22: He said: "Fear not: for I am with you: I hear and see (everything).
trs.203: He (Allâh) said: "Fear not, verily I am with you both, hearing and seeing.

verses.text_uthmani: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ ۖ قَدْ جِئْنَـٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَٱلسَّلَـٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

trs.20: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace<sup foot_note=196748>1</sup> will be upon he who follows the guidance.
trs.85: Go and tell him, “We are your Lord’s mes-sengers, so send the Children of Israel with us and do not oppress them. We have brought you a sign from your Lord. Peace be upon whoever follows the right guidance;
trs.22: "So go ye both to him, and say, 'Verily we are messengers sent by thy Lord: Send forth, therefore, the Children of Israel with us, and afflict them not: with a Sign, indeed, have we come from thy Lord! and peace to all who follow guidance!
trs.203: "So go you both to him, and say: ‘Verily, we are Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance!

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ

trs.20: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.'"
trs.85: it has been revealed to us that punishment falls on whoever rejects the truth and turns his back on it.”’
trs.22: "'Verily it has been revealed to us that the Penalty (awaits) those who reject and turn away.'"
trs.203: "Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies [believes not in the Oneness of Allâh, and in His Messengers.], and turns away (from the truth and obedience of Allâh)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: [Pharaoh] said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"
trs.85: [Pharaoh] said, ‘Moses, who is this Lord of yours?’
trs.22: (When this message was delivered), (Pharaoh) said: "Who, then, O Moses, is the Lord of you two?"
trs.203: Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: "Who then, O Mûsâ (Moses), is the Lord of you two?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ

trs.20: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]."
trs.85: Moses said, ‘Our Lord is He who gave everything its form, then gave it guidance.’
trs.22: He said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each (created) thing its form and nature, and further, gave (it) guidance."
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ

trs.20: [Pharaoh] said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?"
trs.85: He said, ‘What about former generations?’
trs.22: (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the condition of previous generations?"
trs.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "What about the generations of old?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَـٰبٍ ۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى

trs.20: [Moses] said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
trs.85: Moses said, ‘My Lord alone has knowledge of them, all in a record; my Lord does not err or forget.’
trs.22: He replied: "The knowledge of that is with my Lord, duly recorded: my Lord never errs, nor forgets,-
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor He forgets."

verses.text_uthmani: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ

trs.20: [It is He] who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants.
trs.85: It was He who spread out the earth for you and traced routes in it. He sent down water from the sky. With that water We bring forth every kind of plant,
trs.22: "He Who has, made for you the earth like a carpet spread out; has enabled you to go about therein by roads (and channels); and has sent down water from the sky." With it have We produced diverse pairs of plants each separate from the others.
trs.203: Who has made earth for you like a bed (spread out); and has opened roads (ways and paths) for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation.

verses.text_uthmani: كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَـٰمَكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ

trs.20: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
trs.85: so eat, and graze your cattle. There are truly signs in all this for people of understand-ing.
trs.22: Eat (for yourselves) and pasture your cattle: verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
trs.203: Eat and pasture your cattle (therein); verily, in this are Ayât (proofs and signs) for men of understanding.

verses.text_uthmani: ۞ مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَـٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ

trs.20: From it [i.e., the earth] We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.
trs.85: From the earth We created you, into it We shall return you, and from it We shall raise you a second time.
trs.22: From the (earth) did We create you, and into it shall We return you, and from it shall We bring you out once again.
trs.203: Thereof (the earth) We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again.

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَـٰهُ ءَايَـٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ

trs.20: And We certainly showed him [i.e., Pharaoh] Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused.
trs.85: We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he denied them and refused [to change].
trs.22: And We showed Pharaoh all Our Signs, but he did reject and refuse.
trs.203: And indeed We showed him [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] all Our Ayât (signs and evidence), but he denied and refused.

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?
trs.85: He said, ‘Have you come to drive us from our land with your sorcery, Moses?
trs.22: He said: "Hast thou come to drive us out of our land with thy magic, O Moses?
trs.203: He [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Mûsâ (Moses)?

verses.text_uthmani: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى

trs.20: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."<sup foot_note=196749>1</sup>
trs.85: We will confront you with sorcery to match your own: make an appointment between us which neither of us will fail to keep, in a mutually agreeable place.’
trs.22: "But we can surely produce magic to match thine! So make a tryst between us and thee, which we shall not fail to keep - neither we nor thou - in a place where both shall have even chances."
trs.203: "Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (and beholders could witness the competition)."

translation.text: Then we will surely produce for you

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى

trs.20: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."<sup foot_note=196750>1</sup>
trs.85: He said, ‘Your meeting will be on the day of the feast, so let the people be assembled when the sun has risen high.’
trs.22: Moses said: "Your tryst is the Day of the Festival, and let the people be assembled when the sun is well up."
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon)."

verses.text_uthmani: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ

trs.20: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses].
trs.85: Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his resources, then he returned.
trs.22: So Pharaoh withdrew: He concerted his plan, and then came (back).
trs.203: So Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) withdrew, devised his plot and then came back.

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ

trs.20: Moses said to them [i.e., the magicians summoned by Pharaoh], "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allāh or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."
trs.85: Moses said to them, ‘Beware, do not invent lies against God or He will destroy you with His punishment. Whoever invents lies will fail.’
trs.22: Moses said to him: Woe to you! Forge not ye a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you (at once) utterly by chastisement: the forger must suffer frustration!"
trs.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said to them: "Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allâh, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allâh) will fail miserably."

verses.text_uthmani: فَتَنَـٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ

trs.20: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation.
trs.85: So they discussed their plan among themselves, talking secretly,
trs.22: So they disputed, one with another, over their affair, but they kept their talk secret.
trs.203: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret.

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَـٰذَٰنِ لَسَـٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ

trs.20: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way [i.e., religion or tradition].
trs.85: saying, ‘These two men are sorcerers. Their purpose is to drive you out of your land with their sorcery and put an end to your time-honoured way of life.
trs.22: They said: "These two are certainly (expert) magicians: their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to do away with your most cherished institutions.
trs.203: They said: "Verily these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with magic, and overcome your chiefs and nobles.

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّا ۚ وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ

trs.20: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes."
trs.85: So gather your resources and line up for the contest. Whoever wins today is sure to prosper.’
trs.22: "Therefore concert your plan, and then assemble in (serried) ranks: He wins (all along) today who gains the upper hand."
trs.203: "So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ يَـٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ

trs.20: They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw."
trs.85: They said, ‘Moses, will you throw first or shall we?’
trs.22: They said: "O Moses! whether wilt thou that thou throw (first) or that we be the first to throw?"
trs.203: They said: "O Mûsâ (Moses)! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ ۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ

trs.20: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving [like snakes].
trs.85: ‘You throw,’ said Moses, and––lo and behold!––through their sorcery, their ropes and staffs seemed to him to be moving.
trs.22: He said, "Nay, throw ye first!" Then behold their ropes and their rods-so it seemed to him on account of their magic - began to be in lively motion!
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Nay, throw you (first)!" Then behold! their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast.

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ

trs.20: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Moses.
trs.85: Moses was inwardly alarmed,
trs.22: So Moses conceived in his mind a (sort of) fear.
trs.203: So Mûsâ (Moses) conceived fear in himself.

verses.text_uthmani: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ

trs.20: We [i.e., Allāh] said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior.
trs.85: but We said, ‘Do not be afraid, you have the upper hand.
trs.22: We said: "Fear not! for thou hast indeed the upper hand:
trs.203: We (Allâh) said: "Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand.

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَـٰحِرٍ ۖ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ

trs.20: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is."
trs.85: Throw down what is in your right hand: it will swallow up what they have produced. They have only produced the tricks of a sorcerer, and a sorcerer will not prosper, wherever he goes.’
trs.22: "Throw that which is in thy right hand: Quickly will it swallow up that which they have faked what they have faked is but a magician's trick: and the magician thrives not, (no matter) where he goes."
trs.203: "And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician’s trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain."

verses.text_uthmani: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَـٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: So the magicians fell down in prostration.<sup foot_note=196751>1</sup> They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
trs.85: [So it was, and] the sorcerers threw themselves down in submission. ‘We believe,’ they said, ‘in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’
trs.22: So the magicians were thrown down to prostration: they said, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses".
trs.203: So the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Hârûn (Aaron) and Mûsâ (Moses)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ ۖ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَـٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ

trs.20: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Moses] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring."
trs.85: Pharaoh said, ‘How dare you believe in him before I have given you permission? This must be your master, the man who taught you witchcraft. I shall certainly cut off your alternate hands and feet, then crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. You will know for certain which of us has the fiercer and more lasting punishment.’
trs.22: (Pharaoh) said: "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? Surely this must be your leader, who has taught you magic! be sure I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will have you crucified on trunks of palm-trees: so shall ye know for certain, which of us can give the more severe and the more lasting punishment!"
trs.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Believe you in him [Mûsâ (Moses)] before I give you permission? Verily he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms, and you shall surely know which of us [I (Fir‘aun - Pharaoh) or the Lord of Mûsâ (Moses) (Allâh)] can give the severe and more lasting torment."

translation.text: So surely I will cut off
and surely I will crucify you

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا ۖ فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ ۖ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ

trs.20: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us.<sup foot_note=196752>1</sup> So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.
trs.85: They said, ‘We shall never prefer you to the clear sign that has come to us, nor to Him who created us. So decide whatever you will: you can only decide matters of this present life-
trs.22: They said: "Never shall we regard thee as more than the Clear Signs that have come to us, or than Him Who created us! so decree whatever thou desirest to decree: for thou canst only decree (touching) the life of this world.
trs.203: They said: "We prefer you not over what have come to us of the clear signs and to Him (Allâh) Who created us. So decree whatever you desire to decree, for you can only decree (regarding) this life of the world.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَـٰيَـٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

trs.20: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allāh is better and more enduring."<sup foot_note=196753>1</sup>
trs.85: we believe in our Lord, [hoping] He may forgive us our sins and the sorcery that you forced us to practise- God is better and more lasting.’
trs.22: "For us, we have believed in our Lord: may He forgive us our faults, and the magic to which thou didst compel us: for Allah is Best and Most Abiding."
trs.203: "Verily we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allâh is better as regards reward in comparison to your [Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh)] reward, and more lasting (as regards punishment in comparison to your punishment)."

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ

trs.20: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
trs.85: Hell will be the reward of those who return to their Lord as evildoers: there they will stay, neither living nor dying.
trs.22: Verily he who comes to his Lord as a sinner (at Judgment),- for him is Hell: therein shall he neither die nor live.
trs.203: Verily whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, sinner, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allâh and His Messengers), then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live.

verses.text_uthmani: وَمَن يَأْتِهِۦ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَـٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ

trs.20: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position]:
trs.85: But those who return to their Lord as believers with righteous deeds will be rewarded with the highest of ranks,
trs.22: But such as come to Him as Believers who have worked righteous deeds,- for them are ranks exalted,-
trs.203: But whoever comes to Him (Allâh) as a believer (in the Oneness of Allâh), and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (in the Hereafter), -

verses.text_uthmani: جَنَّـٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ

trs.20: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.<sup foot_note=196754>1</sup>
trs.85: Gardens of lasting bliss graced with flowing streams, and there they will stay. Such is the reward of those who purify themselves.
trs.22: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers: they will dwell therein for aye: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (from evil).
trs.203: ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (by abstaining from all kinds of sins and evil deeds which Allâh has forbidden and by doing all that Allâh has ordained).

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَّا تَخَـٰفُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ

trs.20: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."
trs.85: We revealed to Moses, ‘Go out at night with My servants and strike a dry path for them across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken and do not be dismayed.’
trs.22: We sent an inspiration to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, and strike a dry path for them through the sea, without fear of being overtaken (by Pharaoh) and without (any other) fear."
trs.203: And indeed We revealed to Mûsâ (Moses) (saying): "Travel by night with Ibâdi (My slaves) and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] nor being afraid (of drowning in the sea)."

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ

trs.20: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,<sup foot_note=196755>1</sup>
trs.85: Pharaoh pursued them with his armies and was overwhelmed by the sea.
trs.22: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his forces, but the waters completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
trs.203: Then Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) pursued them with his hosts, but the sea-water completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ

trs.20: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
trs.85: Pharaoh truly led his people astray; he did not guide them.
trs.22: Pharaoh led his people astray instead of leading them aright.
trs.203: And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) led his people astray, and he did not guide them.

verses.text_uthmani: يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَـٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَـٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ

trs.20: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you<sup foot_note=196756>1</sup> at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails,
trs.85: Children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemies. We made a pledge with you on the right-hand side of the mountain. We sent down manna and quails for you,
trs.22: O ye Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a Covenant with you on the right side of Mount (Sinai), and We sent down to you Manna and quails:
trs.203: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you Al-Manna <sup foot_note=154716>1</sup> and quails,

translation.text: and We made a covenant with you

verses.text_uthmani: كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَـٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى ۖ وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ

trs.20: [Saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress [or oppress others] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen [i.e., perished]."
trs.85: ‘Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not overstep the bounds, or My wrath will descend on you. Anyone on whom My wrath descends has truly fallen.
trs.22: (Saying): "Eat of the good things We have provided for your sustenance, but commit no excess therein, lest My Wrath should justly descend on you: and those on whom descends My Wrath do perish indeed!
trs.203: (Saying) eat of the Tayyibât (good lawful things) wherewith We have provided you, and commit no transgression or oppression therein, lest My Anger should justly descend on you. And he on whom My Anger descends, he is indeed perished. [Tafsir At-Tabari]

verses.text_uthmani: وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ

trs.20: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
trs.85: Yet I am most forgiving towards those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and stay on the right path.’
trs.22: "But, without doubt, I am (also) He that forgives again and again, to those who repent, believe, and do right, who,- in fine, are ready to receive true guidance."
trs.203: And verily, I am indeed forgiving to him who repents, believes (in My Oneness, and associates none in worship with Me) and does righteous good deeds, and then remains constant in doing them, (till his death).

verses.text_uthmani: ۞ وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh said], "And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?"
trs.85: [God said], ‘Moses, what has made you come ahead of your people in such haste?’
trs.22: (When Moses was up on the Mount, Allah said:) "What made thee hasten in advance of thy people, O Moses?"
trs.203: "And what made you hasten from your people, O Mûsâ (Moses)?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ

trs.20: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased."
trs.85: and he said, ‘They are following in my footsteps. I rushed to You, Lord, to please You,’
trs.22: He replied: "Behold, they are close on my footsteps: I hastened to thee, O my Lord, to please thee."
trs.203: He said: "They are close on my footsteps: and I hastened to You, O my Lord, that You might be pleased."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Sāmirī<sup foot_note=196757>1</sup> has led them astray."
trs.85: but God said, ‘We have tested your people in your absence: the Samiri has led them astray.’
trs.22: (Allah) said: "We have tested thy people in thy absence: the Samiri has led them astray."
trs.203: (Allâh) said: "Verily We have tried your people in your absence, and As-Sâmirî has led them astray."

verses.text_uthmani: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَـٰنَ أَسِفًا ۚ قَالَ يَـٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا ۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى

trs.20: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved.<sup foot_note=196759>1</sup> He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?<sup foot_note=196758>2</sup> Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"
trs.85: Moses returned to his people, angry and aggrieved. He said, ‘My people, did your Lord not make you a gracious promise? Was my absence too long for you? Did you want anger to fall on you from your Lord and so broke your word to me?’
trs.22: So Moses returned to his people in a state of indignation and sorrow. He said: "O my people! did not your Lord make a handsome promise to you? Did then the promise seem to you long (in coming)? Or did ye desire that Wrath should descend from your Lord on you, and so ye broke your promise to me?"
trs.203: Then Mûsâ (Moses) returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow. He said: "O my people! Did not your Lord promise you a fair promise? Did then the promise seem to you long in coming? Or did you desire that wrath should descend from your Lord on you, that you broke your promise to me (i.e disbelieving in Allâh and worshipping the calf)?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَـٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَـٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

trs.20: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Sāmirī throw."
trs.85: They said, ‘We did not break our word to you deliberately. We were burdened with the weight of people’s jewellery, so we threw it [into the fire], and the Samiri did the same,’
trs.22: They said: "We broke not the promise to thee, as far as lay in our power: but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the (whole) people, and we threw them (into the fire), and that was what the Samiri suggested.
trs.203: They said: "We broke not the promise to you, of our own will, but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the [Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh)] people, then we cast them (into the fire), and that was what As-Sâmirî suggested."

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَـٰذَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَـٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ

trs.20: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."
trs.85: but he [used the molten jewellery to] produce an image of a calf which made a lowing sound, and they said, ‘This is your god and Moses’ god, but he has forgotten.’
trs.22: "Then he brought out (of the fire) before the (people) the image of a calf: It seemed to low: so they said: This is your god, and the god of Moses, but (Moses) has forgotten!"
trs.203: Then he took out (of the fire) for them (a statue of) a calf which seemed to low. They said: "This is your ilâh (god), and the ilâh (god) of Mûsâ (Moses), but he [Mûsâ (Moses)] has forgotten (his god).’"

verses.text_uthmani: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا

trs.20: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech [i.e., response] and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit?
trs.85: Did they not see that [the calf] gave them no answer, that it had no power to harm or benefit them?
trs.22: Could they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
trs.203: Did they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَـٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَـٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى

trs.20: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."
trs.85: Aaron did say to them, ‘My people, this calf is a test for you. Your true Lord is the Lord of Mercy, so follow me and obey my orders,’
trs.22: Aaron had already, before this said to them: "O my people! ye are being tested in this: for verily your Lord is (Allah) Most Gracious; so follow me and obey my command."
trs.203: And Hârûn (Aaron) indeed had said to them beforehand: "O my people! You are being tried in this, and verily, your Lord is (Allâh) the Most Gracious, so follow me and obey my order."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَـٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ

trs.20: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it [i.e., the calf] until Moses returns to us."
trs.85: but they replied, ‘We shall not give up our devotion to it until Moses returns to us.’
trs.22: They had said: "We will not abandon this cult, but we will devote ourselves to it until Moses returns to us."
trs.203: They said: "We will not stop worshipping it (i.e. the calf), until Mûsâ (Moses) returns to us."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ يَـٰهَـٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟

trs.20: [Moses] said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
trs.85: Moses said, ‘When you realized they had gone astray, what prevented you, Aaron,
trs.22: (Moses) said: "O Aaron! what kept thee back, when thou sawest them going wrong,
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "O Hârûn (Aaron)! What prevented you when you saw them going astray;

verses.text_uthmani: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ ۖ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى

trs.20: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?"
trs.85: from coming after me? How could you disobey my orders?’
trs.22: "From following me? Didst thou then disobey my order?"
trs.203: "That you followed me not (according to my advice to you)? Have you then disobeyed my order?"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ ۖ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى

trs.20: [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.'"
trs.85: He said, ‘Son of my mother- let go of my beard and my hair!- I was afraid you would say, “You have caused division among the children of Israel and have not heeded what I said.”’
trs.22: (Aaron) replied: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard nor by (the hair of) my head! Truly I feared lest thou shouldst say, 'Thou has caused a division among the children of Israel, and thou didst not respect my word!'"
trs.203: He [Hârûn (Aaron)] said: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard, nor by my head! Verily, I feared lest you should say: ‘You have caused a division among the Children of Israel, and you have not respected my word!’ "

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَـٰسَـٰمِرِىُّ

trs.20: [Moses] said, "And what is your case, O Sāmirī?"
trs.85: Moses said, ‘And what was the matter with you, Samiri?’
trs.22: (Moses) said: "What then is thy case, O Samiri?"
trs.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "And what is the matter with you. O Sâmirî? (i.e. why did you do so?)"

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى

trs.20: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger<sup foot_note=196761>1</sup> and threw it,<sup foot_note=196760>2</sup> and thus did my soul entice me."
trs.85: He replied, ‘I saw something they did not; I took in some of the teachings of the Messenger but tossed them aside: my soul prompted me to do what I did.’
trs.22: He replied: "I saw what they saw not: so I took a handful (of dust) from the footprint of the Messenger, and threw it (into the calf): thus did my soul suggest to me."
trs.203: (Sâmirî) said: "I saw what they saw not, so I took a handful (of dust) from the (hoof) print of the messenger [Jibrîl’s (Gabriel) horse] and threw it [into the fire in which were put the ornaments of Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh) people, or into the calf]. Thus my inner-self suggested to me."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ ۖ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ ۖ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَـٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا ۖ لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

trs.20: [Moses] said, "Then go. And indeed, it is [decreed] for you in [this] life to say, 'No contact.'<sup foot_note=196762>1</sup> And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it [i.e., its ashes] into the sea with a blast.
trs.85: Moses said, ‘Get away from here! Your lot in this life is to say, “Do not touch me,” but you have an appointment from which there is no escape. Look at your god which you have kept on worshipping- we shall grind it down and scatter it into the sea.
trs.22: (Moses) said: "Get thee gone! but thy (punishment) in this life will be that thou wilt say, 'touch me not'; and moreover (for a future penalty) thou hast a promise that will not fail: Now look at thy god, of whom thou hast become a devoted worshipper: We will certainly (melt) it in a blazing fire and scatter it broadcast in the sea!"
trs.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said: "Then go away! And verily, your (punishment) in this life will be that you will say: "Touch me not (i.e. you will live alone exiled away from mankind); and verily (for a future torment), you have a promise that will not fail. And look at your ilâh (god) to which you have been devoted. We will certainly burn it, and scatter its particles in the sea."

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًا

trs.20: Your god is only Allāh, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge."
trs.85: [People], your true god is the One God- there is no god but Him- whose knowledge embraces everything.’
trs.22: But the god of you all is the One Allah: there is no god but He: all things He comprehends in His knowledge.
trs.203: Your Ilâh (God) is only Allâh, (the One) Lâ ilâha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He). He has full knowledge of all things.

verses.text_uthmani: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ ۚ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَـٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًا

trs.20: Thus, [O Muḥammad], We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us a message [i.e., the Qur’ān].
trs.85: In this way We relate to you [Prophet] stories of what happened before. We have given you a Quran from Us.
trs.22: Thus do We relate to thee some stories of what happened before: for We have sent thee a Message from Our own Presence.
trs.203: Thus We relate to you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) some information of what happened before. And indeed We have given you from Us a Reminder (this Qur’ân).

verses.text_uthmani: مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وِزْرًا

trs.20: Whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden [i.e., great sin],
trs.85: Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a heavy burden
trs.22: If any do turn away therefrom, verily they will bear a burden on the Day of judgment;
trs.203: Whoever turns away from it (this Qur’ân - i.e. does not believe in it, nor acts on its orders), verily, they will bear a heavy burden (of sins) on the Day of Resurrection,<sup foot_note=154717>1</sup>

verses.text_uthmani: خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ ۖ وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ حِمْلًا

trs.20: [Abiding] eternally therein,<sup foot_note=196763>1</sup> and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load -
trs.85: and will remain under it. What a terrible burden to carry on that Day!
trs.22: They will abide in this (state): and grievous will the burden be to them on that Day,-
trs.203: They will abide in that (state in the Fire of Hell) - and evil indeed will it be that load for them on the Day of Resurrection;

verses.text_uthmani: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ ۚ وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا

trs.20: The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.<sup foot_note=196764>1</sup>
trs.85: When the trumpet is sounded and We gather the sinful, sightless,
trs.22: The Day when the Trumpet will be sounded: that Day, We shall gather the sinful, blear-eyed (with terror).
trs.203: The Day when the Trumpet will be blown (the second blowing): that Day, We shall gather the Mujrimûn (criminals, polytheists, sinners, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allâh) blue or blind-eyed with thirst.<sup foot_note=154718>1</sup>

verses.text_uthmani: يَتَخَـٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا

trs.20: They will murmur among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days in the world]."
trs.85: they will murmur to one another, ‘You stayed only ten days [on earth]’-
trs.22: In whispers will they consult each other: "Yet tarried not longer than ten (Days);
trs.203: They will speak in a very low voice to each other (saying): "You stayed not longer than ten (days)."

verses.text_uthmani: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا

trs.20: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in manner [i.e., wisdom or speech] will say, "You remained not but one day."
trs.85: We know best what they say- but the more perceptive of them will say, ‘Your stay [on earth] was only a single day.’
trs.22: We know best what they will say, when their leader most eminent in conduct will say: "Ye tarried not longer than a day!"
trs.203: We know very well what they will say, when the best among them in knowledge and wisdom will say: "You stayed no longer than a day!"

verses.text_uthmani: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًا

trs.20: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast.<sup foot_note=196765>1</sup>
trs.85: They ask you [Prophet] about the mountains: say, ‘[On that Day] my Lord will blast them into dust
trs.22: They ask thee concerning the Mountains: say, "My Lord will uproot them and scatter them as dust;
trs.203: And they ask you concerning the mountains: say, "My Lord will blast them and scatter them as particles of dust.

verses.text_uthmani: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا

trs.20: And He will leave it [i.e., the earth] a level plain;
trs.85: and leave a flat plain,
trs.22: "He will leave them as plains smooth and level;
trs.203: "Then He shall leave them as a level smooth plain.

verses.text_uthmani: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَآ أَمْتًا

trs.20: You will not see therein a depression or an elevation."
trs.85: with no peak or trough to be seen.
trs.22: "Nothing crooked or curved wilt thou see in their place."
trs.203: "You will see therein nothing crooked or curved."

verses.text_uthmani: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ ۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا

trs.20: That Day, they [i.e., everyone] will follow [the call of] the Caller<sup foot_note=196766>1</sup> [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps].
trs.85: On that Day, people will follow the summoner from whom there is no escape; every voice will be hushed for the Lord of Mercy; only whispers will be heard.
trs.22: On that Day will they follow the Caller (straight): no crookedness (can they show) him: all sounds shall humble themselves in the Presence of (Allah) Most Gracious: nothing shalt thou hear but the tramp of their feet (as they march).
trs.203: On that Day mankind will follow strictly (the voice of) Allâh’s caller, no crookedness (that is without going to the right or left of that voice) will they show him (Allâh’s caller). And all voices will be humbled for the Most Gracious (Allâh), and nothing shall you hear but the low voice of their footsteps.

verses.text_uthmani: يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَـٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُۥ قَوْلًا

trs.20: That Day, no intercession will benefit except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word.
trs.85: On that Day, intercession will be useless except from those to whom the Lord of Mercy has granted permission and whose words He approves-
trs.22: On that Day shall no intercession avail except for those for whom permission has been granted by (Allah) Most Gracious and whose word is acceptable to Him.
trs.203: On that day no intercession shall avail, except the one for whom the Most Gracious (Allâh) has given permission and whose word is acceptable to Him.

verses.text_uthmani: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًا

trs.20: He [i.e., Allāh] knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them,<sup foot_note=196767>1</sup> but they do not encompass it [i.e., what He knows] in knowledge.
trs.85: He knows what is before and behind them, though they do not comprehend Him-
trs.22: He knows what (appears to His creatures as) before or after or behind them: but they shall not compass it with their knowledge.
trs.203: He (Allâh) knows what happens to them (His creatures) in this world, and what will happen to them (in the Hereafter) but they will never compass anything of His Knowledge.

verses.text_uthmani: ۞ وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا

trs.20: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.<sup foot_note=196769>1</sup> And he will have failed who carries injustice.<sup foot_note=196768>2</sup>
trs.85: and [all] faces will be humbled before the Living, Ever Watchful One. Those burdened with evil deeds will despair,
trs.22: (All) faces shall be humbled before (Him) - the Living, the Self-Subsisting, Eternal: hopeless indeed will be the man that carries iniquity (on his back).
trs.203: And (all) faces shall be humbled before (Allâh), Al-Hayyul-Qayyum (the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists). And he who carried (a burden of) wrongdoing (i.e. he who disbelieved in Allâh, ascribed partners to Him, and did deeds of His disobedience), will be indeed a complete failure (on that Day).

verses.text_uthmani: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا

trs.20: But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
trs.85: but whoever has done righteous deeds and believed need have no fear of injustice or deprivation.’
trs.22: But he who works deeds of righteousness, and has faith, will have no fear of harm nor of any curtailment (of what is his due).
trs.203: And he who works deeds of righteousness, while he is a believer (in Islâmic Monotheism), then he will have no fear of injustice, nor of any curtailment (of his reward).

verses.text_uthmani: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا

trs.20: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān<sup foot_note=196770>1</sup> and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance.
trs.85: We have sent the Quran down in the Arabic tongue and given all kinds of warnings in it, so that they may beware or take heed-
trs.22: Thus have We sent this down - an arabic Qur'an - and explained therein in detail some of the warnings, in order that they may fear Allah, or that it may cause their remembrance (of Him).
trs.203: And thus We have sent it down as a Qur’ân in Arabic, and have explained therein in detail the warnings, in order that they may fear Allâh, or that it may cause them to have a lesson from it (or to have the honour for believing and acting on its teachings).

verses.text_uthmani: فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا

trs.20: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign,<sup foot_note=196772>1</sup> the Truth.<sup foot_note=196771>2</sup> And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
trs.85: exalted be God, the one who is truly in control. [Prophet], do not rush to recite before the revelation is fully complete but say, ‘Lord, increase me in knowledge!’
trs.22: High above all is Allah, the King, the Truth! Be not in haste with the Qur'an before its revelation to thee is completed, but say, "O my Lord! advance me in knowledge."
trs.203: Then High above all be Allâh, the True King. And be not in haste (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) with the Qur’ân before its revelation is completed to you, and say: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge."

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُۥ عَزْمًا

trs.20: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.<sup foot_note=196773>1</sup>
trs.85: We also commanded Adam before you, but he forgot and We found him lacking in constancy.
trs.22: We had already, beforehand, taken the covenant of Adam, but he forgot: and We found on his part no firm resolve.
trs.203: And indeed We made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found on his part no firm will-power.

verses.text_uthmani: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ

trs.20: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees;<sup foot_note=196774>1</sup> he refused.
trs.85: When We said to the angels, ‘Bow down before Adam,’ they did. But Iblis refused,
trs.22: When We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves to Adam", they prostrated themselves, but not Iblis: he refused.
trs.203: And (remember) when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves to Adam." They prostrated themselves (all) except Iblîs (Satan) he refused.

verses.text_uthmani: فَقُلْنَا يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ

trs.20: So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer.
trs.85: so We said, ‘Adam, this is your enemy, yours and your wife’s: do not let him drive you out of the garden and make you miserable.
trs.22: Then We said: "O Adam! verily, this is an enemy to thee and thy wife: so let him not get you both out of the Garden, so that thou art landed in misery.
trs.203: Then We said: "O Adam! Verily, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not get you both out of Paradise, so that you will be distressed.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ

trs.20: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed.
trs.85: In the garden you will never go hungry, feel naked,
trs.22: "There is therein (enough provision) for thee not to go hungry nor to go naked,
trs.203: Verily, you have (a promise from Us) that you will never be hungry therein nor naked.

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ

trs.20: And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be hot from the sun."
trs.85: be thirsty, or suffer the heat of the sun.’
trs.22: "Nor to suffer from thirst, nor from the sun's heat."
trs.203: And you (will) suffer not from thirst therein nor from the sun’s heat.

verses.text_uthmani: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

trs.20: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?"
trs.85: But Satan whispered to Adam, saying, ‘Adam, shall I show you the tree of immortality and power that never decays?’
trs.22: But Satan whispered evil to him: he said, "O Adam! shall I lead thee to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that never decays?"
trs.203: Then Shaitân (Satan) whispered to him, saying: "O Adam! Shall I lead you to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that will never waste away?"

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ

trs.20: And they [i.e., Adam and his wife] ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
trs.85: and they both ate from it. They became conscious of their nakedness and began to cover themselves with leaves from the garden. Adam disobeyed his Lord and was led astray-
trs.22: In the result, they both ate of the tree, and so their nakedness appeared to them: they began to sew together, for their covering, leaves from the Garden: thus did Adam disobey his Lord, and allow himself to be seduced.
trs.203: Then they both ate of the tree, and so their private parts became manifest to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Paradise for their covering. Thus did Adam disobey his Lord, so he went astray.

verses.text_uthmani: ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَـٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ

trs.20: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him].
trs.85: later his Lord brought him close, accepted his repentance, and guided him-
trs.22: But his Lord chose him (for His Grace): He turned to him, and gave him Guidance.
trs.203: Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him with forgiveness, and gave him guidance.

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا ۖ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] said, "Descend from it [i.e., Paradise] - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter].
trs.85: God said, ‘Get out of the garden as each other’s enemy.’ Whoever follows My guidance, when it comes to you [people], will not go astray nor fall into misery,
trs.22: He said: "Get ye down, both of you,- all together, from the Garden, with enmity one to another: but if, as is sure, there comes to you Guidance from Me, whosoever follows My Guidance, will not lose his way, nor fall into misery.
trs.203: He (Allâh) said: "Get you down (from the Paradise to the earth), both of you, together, some of you are an enemy to some others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My Guidance he shall neither go astray, nor shall be distressed.

verses.text_uthmani: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ أَعْمَىٰ

trs.20: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed [i.e., difficult] life, and We will gather [i.e., raise] him on the Day of Resurrection blind."
trs.85: but whoever turns away from it will have a life of great hardship. We shall bring him blind to the Assembly on the Day of Resurrection
trs.22: "But whosoever turns away from My Message, verily for him is a life narrowed down, and We shall raise him up blind on the Day of Judgment."
trs.203: "But whosoever turns away from My Reminder (i.e. neither believes in this Qur’ân nor acts on its teachings.) verily, for him is a life of hardship, and We shall raise him up blind on the Day of Resurrection."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًا

trs.20: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
trs.85: and he will say, ‘Lord, why did You bring me here blind? I was sighted before!’
trs.22: He will say: "O my Lord! why hast Thou raised me up blind, while I had sight (before)?"
trs.203: He will say: "O my Lord! Why have you raised me up blind, while I had sight (before)."

verses.text_uthmani: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ ءَايَـٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا ۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ

trs.20: [Allāh] will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot [i.e., disregarded] them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten."
trs.85: God will say, ‘This is how it is: You ignored Our revelations when they came to you, so today you will be ignored.’
trs.22: (Allah) will say: "Thus didst Thou, when Our Signs came unto thee, disregard them: so wilt thou, this day, be disregarded."
trs.203: (Allâh) will say: "Like this: Our Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) came unto you, but you disregarded them (i.e. you left them, did not think deeply in them, and you turned away from them), and so this Day, you will be neglected (in the Hell-fire, away from Allâh’s Mercy)."

verses.text_uthmani: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ۚ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

trs.20: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.<sup foot_note=196775>1</sup>
trs.85: This is how We reward those who go too far, and who do not believe in their Lord’s revelations. The greatest and most enduring punishment is in the Hereafter.
trs.22: And thus do We recompense him who transgresses beyond bounds and believes not in the Signs of his Lord: and the Penalty of the Hereafter is far more grievous and more enduring.
trs.203: And thus do We requite him who transgresses beyond bounds [i.e. commits the great sins and disobeys his Lord (Allâh) and believes not in His Messengers, and His revealed Books, like this Qur’an], and believes not in the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of his Lord; and the torment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.

verses.text_uthmani: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِى مَسَـٰكِنِهِمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ

trs.20: Then, has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
trs.85: Do they not draw a lesson from the many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwelling places they now walk? There truly are signs in this for anyone with understanding!
trs.22: Is it not a warning to such men (to call to mind) how many generations before them We destroyed, in whose haunts they (now) move? Verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
trs.203: Is it not a guidance for them (to know) how many generations We have destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they walk? Verily, in this are signs indeed for men of understanding.

verses.text_uthmani: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى

trs.20: And if not for a word<sup foot_note=196777>1</sup> that preceded from your Lord, it [i.e., punishment] would have been an obligation [due immediately],<sup foot_note=196776>2</sup> and [if not for] a specified term [decreed].
trs.85: If it were not for a preordained Word from your Lord [Prophet], they would already have been destroyed. Their time has been set,
trs.22: Had it not been for a Word that went forth before from thy Lord, (their punishment) must necessarily have come; but there is a Term appointed (for respite).
